subject: Accounting
title: Accounting Firms Go Global
description: A quick, practical guide to Accounting Firms Go Global.

hook.text: A handful of firms now audit most of the world's biggest companies. They're called the Big Four.

buildup.text: Deloitte, PwC, EY, and KPMG each employ hundreds of thousands of people worldwide.

discovery.text: They started as small local partnerships in the 1800s and merged their way to dominance.

twist.text: There used to be a Big Eight. Mergers and the Enron scandal (Arthur Andersen) shrank it to four.

climax.text: Today the Big Four audit over 80% of all U.S. public companies.

punchline.text: Four firms guard the world's financial trust.

quiz.question: How many firms make up accounting's 'Big Four'?

details.summary: Accounting firms grew from small local practices into global networks during the 20th century, driven by multinational clients who needed consistent audit and advisory services across continents, eventually consolidating into the Big Four.
details.whyItMatters: The globalization of accounting firms shaped how businesses are audited worldwide and created the Big Four firms that now audit the vast majority of the world's largest companies.
takeaways: Multinational clients drove accounting firms to establish offices worldwide in the 20th century
Mergers and consolidation reduced dozens of major firms to today's Big Four
Global firms brought standardized methodology across borders but also concentrated market power

faq.question: How did accounting firms become global?
faq.answer: As businesses expanded internationally in the 20th century, they needed audit firms that could serve them across countries. Accounting firms opened foreign offices, formed international alliances, and merged until the industry consolidated into four dominant global networks.

faq.question: What are the Big Four accounting firms?
faq.answer: The Big Four are Deloitte, PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), Ernst & Young (EY), and KPMG. They audit the majority of large public companies worldwide, employ hundreds of thousands of professionals, and provide audit, tax, and advisory services across virtually every country.
